notes: The page finishes a statement about a correspondence-induced homomorphism between direct-image sheaves and the resulting map on H^1(S, ). Its source coefficient capital is unresolved from ink.

For Y′ a relative curve C and m′=2, the page takes x′ as the degree-2, twist-1 class of the difference of two sections. It states that x′ is primitive when C has geometrically connected fibres and allows any relative divisor of relative degree zero.
It takes Z in degree 2n with twist n on the fibre product Y x_S C, associated to a cycle of codimension n, and discusses restrictions needed for the cycle class to be defined.

Authorial reservation retained: « pour que cette classe de cohomologie soit vraiment définie en l’état actuel de la Science, il faut faire des hypothèses restrictives ». The source gives examples involving finite type over a field, an excellent base of characteristic nulle (clipped), or a relative cycle; none of these claims is proved by transcription.

The relative-cycle condition visibly has ≤ n fibre by fibre. I checked the direction against the ink rather than changing it to a mathematically expected convention. The slanted lower bar is reproduced by leqslant.

Under the stated conditions the page identifies x in degree 2n/twist n with the class of z=Z(t_1)-Z(t_o). The literal round section subscript is ambiguous o|0; this has no role in the conditional degree calculation below.

Authorial reservation retained: « on suppose que les intersections écrites ont un sens », followed by the possibility of using underlined « classes » of cycles. The final hypothesis is retained with the live accent and cancelled-character uncertainties.

The source leaves two long outer NB parentheses unclosed. The inner parenthesis around toujours … Science closes; the earlier relative-degree NB closes after nul. No missing closure or stop is supplied.

All typography decisions were made against this sheet. The earlier notation table was consulted only as comparison: here the three coefficient subscripts independently exhibit the recurring mechanical crossed shape; a literal χ|ℓ uncertainty is retained.

There is no new theorem proof here. The only performed mathematical check is the explicitly conditional local degree computation recorded in check_events; it does not establish the existence or functoriality of the cohomology classes or the full primitivity statement.

Short right-edge slash/dots and pale lower-margin traces lack a secure authorial attachment or alphabet. They are treated as incidental edge/scanning traces under brief v02, not invented as marginal letters or drawings.
No other page, other reader, web source, OCR, text-recognition engine, or published text was accessed.

check_events.outcome: Conditional degree computation only; no formal certificate. Assuming each of the two stated sections meets a geometric fibre as one reduced degree-one point, additivity of the divisor degree gives deg([t_1(s)]-[t_o(s)])=1−1=0. This checks the local degree-zero arithmetic invoked in the paragraph. It does not prove that the divisor class is primitive in the author’s unspecified definition, does not supply missing smoothness/properness hypotheses, and does not construct a cycle class or intersection product.

brief_feedback: v02 is workable. One useful future clarification would distinguish a literal typewriter o-shaped substitute for zero from a semantically read zero when the font supplies no separate zero, and specify how strongly unindented normal-spaced sentence starts should be treated as paragraph boundaries. Missing handwriting wrappers were not collated as H errors; uncertainty and explicit provenance disagreements were recorded.
